title: Clarify SDK cutover & grace-period strategy for pagination, retries, and streaming
creator: Maya Lopez
description: Clarify product and engineering acceptance criteria for a staged SDK cutover that introduces a new pagination/iterator surface, idempotent retry semantics, and clarified streaming reconnection behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This ticket captures scope, constraints, compatibility guarantees, migration windows, required test suites, and rollout gates for a gradual rollforward strategy that minimizes customer disruption while enabling future runtime optimizations.
background: We have multiple feature requests and internal runtime changes that require slight API surface changes in SDKs: explicit resume tokens for pagination, documented idempotent retry semantics for generation requests, and a consistent streaming reconnect/backoff contract. Historically we relied on ad-hoc client behavior; with Dedicated and Private use-cases growing, we need deterministic semantics to support retries, caching, and routing optimizations on the server-side. Several earlier PMs touched client resume semantics but did not finalize migration windows or acceptance tests.
scope: In scope: PRD-level acceptance criteria for Python/TS/Go SDKs; definition of new iterator interface (resume token + stable offset), retry idempotency guarantees, streaming reconnect/backoff contract and default policies, migration guide content, e2e test matrix, and rollout gates. Out of scope: implementation work in each SDK (will be separate ENG tickets), runtime kernel-level changes, and long-term ergonomics iterations post-cutover.
out_of_scope: SDK implementation pull requests, language-specific stylistic changes, any UI/console changes, and changes to billing semantics.
requirements: Unified iterator API across SDKs that supports both offset cursors and opaque resume tokens
Backwards-compatible adapters: old cursor-based pagination continues to work for at least 6 months after GA
Define explicit idempotency key and retry semantics for text-generation and chat endpoints; SDKs must expose a retry policy allowing at-least-once and at-most-once options
Streaming API: explicit reconnection handshake and resume window (default 30s of buffered events) and transparent partial-message reassembly
Default retry/backoff policy aligned across languages: exponential backoff with jitter, configurable max attempts, default max_attempts=5
SDKs must ship a migration guide and a code sample for converting existing paginated loops to the new iterator pattern
Compatibility flagging: SDKs expose a runtime feature flag to opt into new behavior (e.g., client.enable_new_iterators = true) for 1st-party rollouts
Telemetry: SDKs must emit telemetry events for migration usage (opt-in by default) and for retry counts to aid release gating
Interoperability tests: standardized test harness that validates resume token correctness when server-side caching/batching is enabled
Performance baseline: pagination and streaming latency/throughput must be within 10% of current SDK behavior in the typical PLG workload profile
acceptance_criteria: Product: Written PRD section that details migration window (minimum 6 months), deprecation notice cadence, and recommended customer communication templates
Engineering: Shared test harness (language-neutral) that validates resume tokens and idempotency across a matrix of page sizes, token expirations, and intermittent network failures
SDKs: Python/TS/Go SDKs provide a public API surface that matches the PRD signatures (resumeToken in iterator constructor, retryPolicy object, streaming.reconnect(options))
Backward compatibility: Existing code using legacy cursor iteration continues to succeed without code changes for the announced warranty window and passes compatibility smoke tests
Rollout gates: Canary usage metrics (retry rates, resume failures) are defined and observability dashboards are created in Console with alert thresholds
Migration docs: Developer guides and 3 language-specific examples are published in the docs site and linked in the release notes
QA: Automated e2e tests covering: (a) generator retry with idempotency key preserved, (b) iterator resume after transient server restart, (c) streaming reconnect with partial message reassembly
Performance: Benchmarks show no more than 10% regression in p50 token latency for paginated flows compared to current stable SDK release
Sign-off: PM, two SDK maintainers (one per ecosystem), and reliability lead have approved the PRD and acceptance criteria
risks: Customers with custom cursor parsing could break if opaque tokens are adopted without clear migration guidance
Telemetry opt-in might under-report problems during early canaries leading to blind spots
Server-side caching/kv expiry semantics could invalidate resume tokens faster than clients expect
Language SDK implementation divergence if we don't define small canonical bindings and test harnesses
test_plan: Create language-agnostic test harness that can be invoked by SDK CI (Docker image + simple control-plane mock)
E2E test scenarios for resume token replays, token expiry handling, and race conditions during retries
Load test to validate pagination throughput with new iterator surface under typical PLG traffic patterns
Integration tests that exercise streaming reconnect with partial chunking and out-of-order fragments
rollout_strategy: Staged rollout: (1) internal SDK alpha with feature flag enabled, (2) external canary cohorts (5-10 customers) with enhanced telemetry, (3) gradual increase in opt-in customers via SDK default off but easy opt-in, (4) opt-in default flipped after 6-week canary and metric validation, (5) deprecation announcement and 6-month compatibility window before removing legacy adapter
metrics_and_gates: no increase in 5xx errors upstream attributable to SDK retries during canary
docs_and_communications: Migration guide article: code samples for Python/TS/Go, FAQ, troubleshooting
Deprecation timeline blog post and email templates for account owners
Release notes with explicit flags and snippet for rolling back to legacy behavior
Internal runbook for SREs describing how to detect and mitigate resume token regressions
notes: Favor minimal surface change in first cut: expose resumeToken but keep common helper adapters for legacy usage
Coordinate announcement with Dedicated account managers and Platform PMs to avoid surprises for Reserved customers
Consider short-term compatibility shim in server that accepts both token types for the migration window
